summary: A paper by Shoshani and Spiegler on integrating data management systems on a computer network, so that data held in different systems could be reached together. It is an early discussion of the idea rather than a protocol specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This paper explores how users might query data held in different management systems across a network. It proposes a common language that translator interfaces convert for each system.

subtitle: A common-language approach to sharing data across management systems.

tldr.problem: Different data management systems use different languages, making it difficult to share data across a computer network.
tldr.mechanism: The paper proposes a common language and translator interfaces that convert requests to each system's data language.
tldr.outcome: It describes ILDS and experiments with translators, while presenting integration as an approach for investigation.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 500's status as Unknown. The paper presents an approach to integrating data management systems, not a network protocol specification.

sections.title: Sharing Data Across Systems
sections.content:
Shoshani and Spiegler discuss integrating data management systems on a computer network to share data. They note that duplicating large databases can be expensive and restructuring data for different applications can be difficult.

The paper chooses an integrated approach intended to let existing systems and databases continue operating while users gain another way to access them.
sections.plainLanguage: Organizations may keep useful data in different systems. The paper explores sharing it without replacing each existing system.

sections.title: A Common Language and Translator Interfaces
sections.content:
In the proposed design, a user sends a request in a common language. An interface associated with a data management system translates the request into that system's language, and the system performs the requested work.

The paper considers interfaces located with each data system or collected at a central node. It also discusses translating results into a common format when replies from multiple systems need to be combined.
sections.plainLanguage: The user writes a request in one shared language. A translator changes it into the language used by the selected data system.

sections.title: ILDS and Its Operations
sections.content:
The paper describes ILDS, the Intermediate Language for Data Sharing, for hierarchical data structures. Its kernel includes create, delete, update, and query operations; qualifiers select entries, while output and replacement functions return or change values.

The authors also describe experimental translators to two data management languages built using a meta-compiler. The paper reports that each translator took about two to three person-months to implement and debug.
sections.plainLanguage: ILDS describes operations such as selecting entries, returning values, and changing data. The paper reports experiments translating this language into two existing systems.
